messages:
maya.prod: Hey team — onboarding blocked for AcuHealth. Their Node SDK is getting intermittent 401 then a bunch of 429s during staging load tests. Started ~09:10 UTC. Anyone seen this pattern?

aisha_cs: Sorry you're hitting this, maya. Can you paste the SDK logs around a failed request? 401 then 429 is usually a token refresh + retry fanout symptom. :thinking:

maya.prod: Log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-21T09:10:05Z] auth: refresh token request -> 200
[2026-03-21T09:10:05Z] request: POST /v1/generate -> 401 {"err":"jwt not yet valid"}
[2026-03-21T09:10:06Z] auth: refresh token retry -> 200
[2026-03-21T09:10:06Z] request: POST /v1/generate -> 429 {"err":"rate_limit.exceeded"}
```
We also see a bunch of parallel lambda cold starts. They said they do ephemeral token per invocation (company policy).

ben_ingram: Two signals here: the 401 is "nbf" (not before) / clock skew issue, then many parallel instances refresh and immediately hit the API with no jitter -> brief surge triggers 429s. Could be SSO provider issuing tokens with slight future nbf (or client clock off).

aisha_cs: Can you check the token payload? Example: `jwt.decode(token)` and look at `iat`/`nbf`/`exp`. If `nbf` > now by a few seconds it's the issue.

maya.prod: Decoded payload: `nbf: 1711060206`, `iat: 1711060206`, `exp: 1711063806`. Our server time is 5s behind.

sam_oncall: That aligns. NTP drift on their container hosts + SSO token issued with tight timing = 401 until clock catches up. Meanwhile all lambdas refresh and flood the service.

ben_ingram: Short-term mitigations:
- Add small client-side clock tolerance when validating tokens (e.g., allow 10s skew) or set `clockTolerance` in JWT lib.
- Introduce randomized jitter on token refresh across concurrent workers (add 50-300ms randomized delay).
- Limit concurrent refreshes via an in-process token mutex or shared cache (fetch-once pattern).

maya.prod: We control the customer infra? They use Fargate with custom AMI. Ops says NTP drift on image is possible. They'll patch. Meanwhile can we recommend SDK changes?

aisha_cs: Yes, recommend these SDK changes in docs/email:
```
// Node example: single-refresh guard + jitter
let refreshInProgress = null;
async function getToken() {
  if (refreshInProgress) return await refreshInProgress;
  refreshInProgress = (async () => {
    await sleep(Math.random() * 250); // jitter
    const t = await fetchNewToken();
    refreshInProgress = null;
    return t;
  })();
  return await refreshInProgress;
}
```
Also set `jwt.verify(token, {clockTolerance: 10})` when validating locally.

ben_ingram: On our side, we can add a short implicit grace for tokens with tiny nbf offsets (<=10s) and ensure our rate limiter treats quick repeated retries from same client fingerprint as a single throttling event (smarter aggregation). I've flagged infra.

maya.prod: Client will try the SDK patch and NTP fix. Any recommendations for temporary server-side rate handling so they don't hit 429s repeatedly?

sam_oncall: We can return `Retry-After` header (already implemented) but we can also increase short-term burst allowance on their account while they remediate. Will need approval from billing.

aisha_cs: I'll open a support ticket to grant a 30s soft-burst window and email billing. Also adding a short troubleshooting checklist to onboarding playbook. Action items: 1) Customer: enable NTP on hosts (maya), 2) Customer: deploy SDK single-refresh + jitter patch (maya), 3) Redwood infra: temporary burst allowance (aisha), 4) Redwood eng: small token nbf grace + smarter aggregation (ben). Owners and ETA?

maya.prod: I'll get ops to patch NTP today, push SDK change to staging now, report back by 15:30 UTC.

aisha_cs: I filed ticket CS-98321 to billing for burst window. Sam, can you approve?

sam_oncall: Approved for 24h 2x burst. Noted.

ben_ingram: I'll queue a small config change for token nbf tolerance and aggregation; won't be auto-deployed to prod without review but will push a canary by EOD.

maya.prod: Thanks all. After SDK patch staging saw no 401/429 cascade on a 300-invocation spike.

aisha_cs: Great — I'll update the onboarding checklist with a brief section: "If you see 401 then 429 during onboarding: check client clock, use single-refresh with jitter, consider ephemeral token caching, request temporary burst." Will follow up on the billing ticket and close thread when burst window confirmed. :white_check_mark:

ben_ingram: Adding a quick note to our DevEx docs about common SSO-issued nbf quirks and recommended clock tolerance.

token-bot: AUTO: CS-98321 assigned to aisha_cs, priority: high, due: 2026-03-22T09:00:00Z

maya.prod: Closing loop — ops fixed NTP and SDK guard rolled into prod. No further 429s after 24h. Thanks team! :raised_hands:
